newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber end mostly easier in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber end mostly easier in light trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed mostly easier on Wednesday in light, listless trading with the absence of buyers weighing heavily on the market, dealers said.
"It's still a bear market. There's no opportunity for the prices to move up because the offtake is almost not there at all," a local rubber trader said.
Another trader added: "Ring session activity was virtually zero. It's just very, very quiet."
Japan failed to inspire the market despite an increase in Tokyo's benchmark February contract, which closed 1.4 yen higher at 139.3, traders said.
"It was basically flat all-around and I'm not optimistic the situation is going to change tomorrow," another dealer said.
November RSS3 was seen steady at 128.00 U.S. cents a kg at around 0945 GMT.
November RSS1 was seen at 184.25 Singapore cents (US$1.36) a kg against last Tuesday's settlement of 184.50 cents.
November TSR20 was seen at 177.50 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg against 178.00 cents.
